blocks.passage:
A bank guarantee is another kind of promise from a bank. It says: if our customer does not do what they promised, we will pay you instead.

It is useful when one company wants another to trust them. For example, a supplier may ask for a guarantee before starting a big project. If the buyer fails to pay, the bank will.

The guarantee does not replace the deal. It simply adds a safety net, so the two sides can do business with confidence.

items.q: What does a bank guarantee say?
options: If our customer does not do what they promised, we will pay you instead
items.why: "if our customer does not do what they promised, we will pay you instead."

items.q: When is a bank guarantee useful?
options: When one company wants another to trust them
items.why: "It is useful when one company wants another to trust them."

items.q: In the example, who might ask for a guarantee?
options: A supplier, before starting a big project
items.why: "a supplier may ask for a guarantee before starting a big project."

items.q: Does a guarantee replace the deal?
options: No, it adds a safety net
items.why: "The guarantee does not replace the deal. It simply adds a safety net."

items.q: What is the purpose of the safety net?
options: So the two sides can do business with confidence
items.why: "so the two sides can do business with confidence."

audio.text:
Your new buyer in Asia is asking for a performance guarantee before they sign the contract, and you're wondering why. Let me explain — it's actually a normal, fair request.

Think about it from their side. They've never worked with you. They're about to sign a big contract and depend on you to deliver. What if you don't? What if the goods never come, or come late and wrong? They'd be stuck.

So they ask your bank for a performance guarantee. It's a promise: if you, the supplier, don't perform — don't deliver as agreed — the bank pays them instead. It protects them if you fail.

Now, this is not an insult. It doesn't mean they think you'll fail. It's just how careful companies protect themselves with a new partner. Big buyers ask for this all the time.

And here's the good news: once you deliver well on this contract, they'll trust you, and next time they probably won't ask for one at all. The guarantee is really just a bridge of trust for the first deal.

items.q: What is the buyer asking for before signing?
items.why: "Your new buyer in Asia is asking for a performance guarantee."

items.q: Why does the buyer want it?
options: They've never worked with you and depend on you to deliver
items.why: "They've never worked with you… What if you don't [deliver]?"

items.q: What does the performance guarantee promise?
options: If the supplier doesn't deliver as agreed, the bank pays the buyer instead
items.why: "if you, the supplier, don't perform… the bank pays them instead."

items.q: Is the request an insult, according to Sophie?
options: No — it's how careful companies protect themselves with a new partner
items.why: "this is not an insult… It's just how careful companies protect themselves with a new partner."

items.q: What is the 'good news' at the end?
options: Once you deliver well, they'll trust you and probably won't ask next time
items.why: "once you deliver well… next time they probably won't ask for one at all."

items.q: A **bank guarantee** is…
options: a bank's promise to pay if its customer fails to do what they promised
items.why: Bank guarantee = garantia bancária.

items.q: A **safety net** is…
options: protection in case something goes wrong
items.why: Safety net = rede de segurança.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "If the buyer **___** to pay, the bank will pay instead."
items.why: To fail = falhar.

items.q: The **beneficiary** of a guarantee is…
items.why: Beneficiary = beneficiário.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A **performance** guarantee protects the buyer if the supplier does not **___**."
items.why: Performance = cumprimento/entrega do combinado.

items.q: "The guarantee is a **bridge of trust**." A bridge of trust means…
options: something that helps two sides trust each other
items.why: Bridge of trust = ponte de confiança.

items.q: "It's normal — big buyers ask for this **all the time**." All the time means…
items.why: All the time = o tempo todo, com frequência.

items.q: "Think about it **from their side**." From their side means…
items.why: From their side = do ponto de vista deles.

items.q: "If you don't deliver, they'd be **stuck**." To be stuck means to…
options: be in a difficult position with no easy way out
items.why: Be stuck = ficar preso, em apuros.

items.q: "Once you **deliver well**, they'll trust you." To deliver well means to…
items.why: Deliver well = cumprir bem o combinado.
